catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) runner, knowledge repository, governance engines, and agent workflow specifications.
analysis_limits: Repository includes architectural markdown documentation and Python implementation packages
Analysis focused on src/cas_runner and cas-knowledge governance structures

system_map.overview: CAS (Continuous Architecture System) coordinates human and AI agents in architectural decision-making, using declarative knowledge repositories, structured capability steering indices, automated compliance verification, and deterministic execution runners.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Resolves governance conflicts and merges evolving architectural manifests, capability records, and decision templates into active state.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural state transitions, enforces transition contracts, and dispatches governance actions.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Validates runtime execution against schema rules, architectural policies, and governance constraints.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Executes multi-step agentic workflows and orchestrates steering index compilation and validation pipelines.

orchestration.description: Combines a sequential deterministic FlowRunner pipeline with declarative event-driven governance state transitions and LLM-assisted conflict resolution.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Unified abstraction layer for invoking diverse LLM providers with consistent retry, streaming, and error normalization.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Collects distributed spans, prompt latency, and traceable decision metrics during workflow execution.

tools_and_integrations.name: Git & Steering Projection System
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Tracks delta changes in architecture and compiles prompt facts for agent steering context.

state_and_memory.description: File-backed architecture knowledge repository (cas-knowledge) organizing global models, decisions, patterns, signals, and rules in structured markdown/YAML.
Compiled SteeringRuntimeIndex generated from Git deltas and architectural templates, supplying targeted PromptFacts to active agents.
Runtime traces, health status, and compliance findings generated during a single validation or merger execution pass.

patterns.name: Steering Runtime Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects facts and constraints via dynamic compilation rather than runtime tool calls

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agents receive bounded context directly relevant to the modified capabilities.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Compiles relevant constraints deterministically before agent invocation, limiting prompt bloat and divergence.

patterns.summary: Compiles architectural deltas and capability records into a structured runtime index that projects contextual PromptFacts into agent environments.
patterns.intent: Ensure AI agents operate within architectural boundaries by projecting exact governance constraints and delta context into runtime prompts.
patterns.context: Agent execution across repositories requiring strict compliance with architectural decision records and evolving capability models.
forces: Full architecture specifications exceed context window limits and introduce irrelevant noise
Agents without explicit steering violate enterprise architectural standards and conventions
patterns.solution: Compile modified capability lineage and raw Git deltas into a SteeringRuntimeIndex containing indexed PromptFacts that parameterize downstream agent prompts.
implementation_signals: SteeringRuntimeIndex model aggregating CapabilitySet and ArchitecturalDelta
PromptFact model with category and fact lineage
Compilation workflow generating index files prior to agent execution

evidence.note: Defines runtime data models for projecting capability facts into agent steering context.
Automated workflow projecting steering facts from architecture deltas.

benefits: Reduces prompt hallucination and architectural drift
Isolates agent context to only relevant capability boundaries
costs: Requires pre-computation pipeline before agent runs
Index schemas must be maintained alongside capability model changes
failure_modes: Stale index projections lead agents to make decisions based on outdated architectural rules

patterns.reuse_notes: Adaptable to any agentic system where agents must obey structural governance or domain boundaries stored in Git.

patterns.name: Provider-Agnostic LLM Gateway

tool_protocols.notes: Centralizes model invocations behind standardized client wrapper

optimisation_targets.notes: Decouples agent logic from specific vendor SDKs and enables mock testing.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Standardizes call signature across all inference backends.

patterns.summary: Encapsulates LLM inference behind a unified client interface with mock fallbacks for deterministic evaluation and provider flexibility.
patterns.intent: Shield agent logic from vendor-specific LLM APIs while facilitating offline mock testing and runtime provider switching.
patterns.context: Agent runner requiring multi-model support and repeatable continuous integration tests without live API dependencies.
forces: Direct vendor SDK coupling locks the system into single providers and complicates rate-limit handling
Live API calls in CI/CD pipelines introduce flakiness, cost, and non-determinism
patterns.solution: Implement a LiteLLMClient facade backed by a parallel MockLLMClient adhering to the same interface contract.
implementation_signals: LiteLLMClient wrapper abstracting model completions
MockLLMClient implementation for unit and pipeline tests
Dependency on litellm in pyproject.toml

evidence.note: Production LLM client wrapping litellm.
Mock client providing deterministic responses for tests.

benefits: Seamless switching between local, open-source, and proprietary LLMs
Fast, offline unit and integration tests without network I/O
costs: Gateway layer can lag behind novel provider-specific parameters or cutting-edge features
failure_modes: Mock client behavior diverges from actual production LLM response shapes

patterns.reuse_notes: Directly reusable across agentic projects requiring testability and provider independence.

patterns.name: Declarative State Machine Governance

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions evaluate registered rules and gate agent actions

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized or invalid transitions in architecture artifact lifecycle.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Constrains agent autonomy using deterministic state transition tables.

patterns.summary: Enforces valid agent lifecycle state transitions through an explicit transition registry and governance action engine.
patterns.intent: Prevent agents from executing arbitrary or illegal mutations on architecture artifacts by verifying transitions against a declarative registry.
patterns.context: Agent-driven architecture lifecycle management where decisions, rules, and patterns transition from proposal to active governance.
forces: Unchecked autonomous agents can skip required review or validation steps
Hardcoded transition logic scattered across agent scripts becomes brittle and impossible to audit
patterns.solution: Define an explicit TransitionRegistry that validates incoming GovernanceAction events and executes transitions through a dedicated GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class tracking legal state pairs
GovernanceAction and GovernanceException typed models
GovernanceActionService dispatching verified state updates

evidence.note: Registry and execution engine governing permissible state changes.
Service coordinating action invocation against the governance model.
Typed definitions of governance action intents and exceptions.

benefits: Guarantees that agents cannot bypass lifecycle constraints
Auditable, deterministic history of all state changes
costs: Requires formal registration of every valid workflow step and state mutation
failure_modes: Overly restrictive transitions block valid agent remediation paths without human override

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any agentic platform managing compliance, document approval, or deployment pipelines.

patterns.name: Agentic Conflict Resolution Merger

tool_protocols.notes: Uses LLM synthesis to reconcile conflicting schema definitions and git deltas

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates the synthesis of concurrent architectural changes.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Delegates complex semantic reconciliation to an LLM agent within structured constraints.

patterns.summary: Delegates semantic reconciliation of concurrent architectural and code delta conflicts to a specialized merger agent.
patterns.intent: Resolve non-trivial structural and semantic merge conflicts in architectural decisions and schema definitions where textual 3-way merge fails.
patterns.context: Multi-agent or multi-developer workflows concurrently submitting changes to cas-knowledge repositories.
forces: Standard git merges fail on semantic conflicts in structured documents like ADRs or capability sets
Human review for every minor divergence creates severe workflow bottlenecks
patterns.solution: Deploy an AgenticMerger component that takes RawGitDeltas and GovernanceInventory state, prompts an LLM with semantic reconciliation rules, and outputs a ResolutionResult.
implementation_signals: AgenticMerger class orchestrating conflict resolution
ResolutionResult data model indicating success, rationale, and resulting payload
Integration with steering models and delta tracking

evidence.note: Orchestrates semantic resolution of git deltas against governance models.
Typed contract for resolution outputs including status and delta changes.

benefits: Automates synthesis of complex structured artifacts without manual intervention
Preserves architectural intent across disparate branch modifications
costs: Risk of incorrect semantic compromises in critical architecture definitions
Inference latency added during merge operations
failure_modes: Hallucinated reconciliations that introduce subtle inconsistencies into the knowledge base

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be integrated into GitOps PR automation or multi-agent shared state convergence loops.

patterns.name: Traceable Metric Evaluation Loop

tool_protocols.notes: Records evaluation findings and health metrics during execution passes

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures every agent step is audited against compliance rules and traceable.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Systematic automated scoring ensures deterministic evaluation without agent self-grading bias.

patterns.summary: Computes traceable compliance and health metrics during execution runs to monitor architectural health and guardrail violations.
patterns.intent: Quantify agent compliance, execution health, and architectural risk using structured, auditable metric models.
patterns.context: Continuous governance pipeline checking whether system state satisfies codified architectural principles.
forces: Unstructured agent logs provide poor auditability and cannot trigger automated circuit breakers
Subjective or narrative evaluations cannot be reliably trended or visualized on dashboards
patterns.solution: Generate structured ComplianceFinding items, calculate health indicators via calculate_health, and attach TraceableMetric instances to the run output.
implementation_signals: TraceableMetric and ComplianceFinding Pydantic models
ComplianceEngine inspecting rule-context against runtime profiles
HealthStatus scoring in dashboard/health_model.py

evidence.note: Evaluates compliance rules against runtime facts.
Typed models representing quantitative governance and health metrics.
Calculates health categories and diagnoses underlying failure causes.

benefits: Provides immediate numeric and diagnostic signals of architectural drift
Enables automated CI/CD blocking on compliance failures
costs: Requires comprehensive rule specifications in rule-context.json
failure_modes: Incomplete rule coverage allowing silent architectural degradations to pass unchecked

patterns.reuse_notes: Easily ported to CI validation pipelines or guardrail verification agents in any software delivery lifecycle.

patterns.name: File-Backed Blackboard Knowledge Base

tool_protocols.notes: Agents read and write structured markdown/YAML documents in a version-controlled hierarchy

optimisation_targets.notes: Human-readable Git-backed memory ensures versioning and transparency.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Leverages Git for persistence, diffing, and rollbacks rather than opaque vector databases.

patterns.summary: Maintains long-term shared architectural memory as a version-controlled, file-backed hierarchy of markdown and YAML templates.
patterns.intent: Provide a shared, transparent, and auditable memory store where human architects and autonomous agents asynchronously collaborate.
patterns.context: Repository wide storage of decisions, patterns, signals, and rules across global and project-specific namespaces.
forces: Vector databases can be opaque, difficult to audit, and prone to silent retrieval failures
Agents need consistent schema templates to create well-formed architectural deliverables
patterns.solution: Organize knowledge in a disciplined file tree (cas-knowledge/) governed by markdown/YAML templates (ADRs, patterns, rules, signals) backed by Git.
implementation_signals: Dedicated cas-knowledge/ tree partitioned into global/, governance/, projects/, and runtime/
Standardized templates for patterns, rules, signals, and promotion decisions
Workspace initialization and bootstrap routines in bootstrap.py

evidence.note: Standardized schema template for architecture patterns.
Standardized schema template for governance rules.
Initializes and maintains file-backed governance structures.

benefits: Human-inspectable and version-controlled via familiar Git workflows
No external database dependencies needed for agent knowledge retrieval
costs: File system operations and Git syncing can become a bottleneck at large scale
Requires strict linting to maintain template integrity
failure_modes: Template drift causing agent parsing failures if schemas are updated without migration

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal for software engineering, architecture, and governance agents where Git is the system of record.

patterns.name: Sequential Flow Pipeline Orchestration

tool_protocols.notes: Linear execution flow passing immutable context between stages

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees predictable execution ordering for validation and build stages.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Prefers deterministic step-by-step pipeline execution over autonomous unconstrained agent loops.

patterns.summary: Executes complex governance and build workflows through a deterministic pipeline coordinator passing shared state across steps.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-stage architectural evaluation and generation tasks deterministically without allowing unconstrained dynamic loops.
patterns.context: Automated workflow execution for validation, steering projection, and documentation generation.
forces: Unconstrained dynamic agent planning frequently produces infinite loops or non-deterministic step ordering
Architecture governance requires strict ordering (e.g., validate rules before updating portal state)
patterns.solution: Implement FlowRunner to drive discrete steps sequentially, propagating execution profiles and accumulating traceable results.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner coordinator in src/cas_runner/runner.py
CLI entry point invoking FlowRunner pipelines in cli.py
Declarative GitHub workflows orchestrating steps sequentially

evidence.note: Main pipeline runner coordinating execution flows.
CLI triggering runner sequences.
Documentation specifying the sequential automated run stages.

benefits: Clear debugging and rollback boundaries per step
costs: Inflexible when dealing with unexpected failures requiring runtime re-planning
failure_modes: A failure in an early pipeline step aborts downstream governance reporting

patterns.reuse_notes: Foundational pattern for CI/CD-integrated agent runners and enterprise pipeline automation.

patterns.name: Heuristic to Pattern Promotion Lifecycle

tool_protocols.notes: Promotion governed by documented criteria and template fulfillment

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents premature formalization of unverified heuristics into strict enterprise patterns.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Requires human-agent consensus and multi-instance empirical evidence before promotion.

patterns.summary: Governs the progressive promotion of emerging agentic heuristics into validated architectural patterns through explicit threshold criteria.
patterns.intent: Allow agents and architects to capture tentative heuristics quickly while guarding against premature formalization of unverified patterns.
patterns.context: Agent learning loop where observations from multiple runs accumulate in cas-knowledge.
forces: Rigid pattern documentation slows down rapid capture of emergent agentic learnings
Unvetted agent practices promoted to patterns introduce anti-patterns into organizational memory
patterns.solution: Establish a progressive lifecycle template (heuristic-to-pattern_template.md and promotion_decision.md) requiring evidence across multiple contexts before upgrading a heuristic to a mature pattern.
implementation_signals: heuristic-to-pattern_template.md defining transition criteria
promotion_decision.md recording justification and consensus
Documentation in docs/architecture/cas-pattern-evolution-flow.md

evidence.note: Template defining requirements for promoting a heuristic to a pattern.
Template recording formal promotion review and decision rationale.
Workflow detailing pattern lifecycle stages.

benefits: Low friction for capturing early insights, high rigor for institutional adoption
Empirical grounding for all established architectural patterns
costs: Requires periodic manual or semi-automated review passes to process candidates
failure_modes: Heuristic stagnation where valuable insights accumulate in draft states without being reviewed

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to continuous improvement loops and knowledge accumulation in enterprise AI agents.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Agent Merge Autonomy
symptoms: AgenticMerger committing reconciled artifacts directly to production branch without mandatory compliance re-evaluation
No explicit human escalation trigger when merge resolution confidence score is marginal

where_observed.note: Merger relies on prompt instructions but lacks hard circuit breakers if conflict ambiguity is high.

impact: Silent drift in core governance rules or architectural decisions
Potential loss of security or compliance constraints due to LLM hallucination
suggested_remediation: Require ComplianceEngine re-validation immediately following any AgenticMerger resolution prior to persistence.
Add a strict confidence threshold that forces human escalation if resolution ambiguity exceeds limits.

anti_patterns.name: Monolithic Rule Context Injection
symptoms: Loading the complete global rule-context.json into agent prompts regardless of the specific capability being modified
Increased token usage and prompt latency as rule sets grow

where_observed.note: Centralized rule JSON holding global constraints across multiple domains.

impact: Context window exhaustion and higher inference costs
Degraded agent adherence to critical rules due to in-context distraction from irrelevant rules
suggested_remediation: Use SteeringRuntimeIndex to selectively project only capability-scoped rules into the active prompt facts.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Defined through structured Pydantic models (PromptFact, CapabilityRecord) and markdown templates that format factual context prior to LLM submission.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Ensures prompt inputs adhere to schema boundaries rather than unvalidated text concatenation.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Decoupled compliance evaluation executed by ComplianceEngine checking rule-context.json and scoring health metrics.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Prevents agents from grading their own homework by executing evaluation externally in the runner pipeline.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Integrated OpenTelemetry SDK alongside TraceableMetric structures linking governance outcomes to execution traces.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Facilitates post-run auditing and tracing across LLM provider invocations.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent AgenticMerger executions guarded against race conditions during simultaneous Git branch pushes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Simultaneous merges could overwrite resolved state or cause Git tree divergence if locking is omitted.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Repository shows AgenticMerger logic and GitHub workflows, but explicit distributed locking mechanisms are not evident in the codebase.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect GitHub Actions concurrency settings in .github/workflows/cas-continuous-architecture.yml and Git remote push handling.
